Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy. Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs sunlight, primarily in the red and blue wavelengths. Water is split into oxygen, protons, and electrons in the light-dependent reactions. The resulting energy carriers, ATP and NADPH, power the Calvin cycle, which fixes carbon dioxide into glucose.

energy carriers, ATP and NADPH, power the Calvin cycle, which fixes carbon dioxide into glucose. Oxygen is released as a byproduct through small pores called stomata. This process is fundamental to life on Earth, as it forms the base of most food chains and replenishes atmospheric oxygen.

प्रकाश संश्लेषण वह प्रक्रिया है जिसके द्वारा हरे पौधे, शैवाल और कुछ जीवाणु प्रकाश ऊर्जा को रासायनिक ऊर्जा में बदलते हैं। क्लोरोफिल सूर्य के प्रकाश को अवशोषित करता है और जल को ऑक्सीजन, प्रोटॉन और इलेक्ट्रॉन में विभाजित करता है। इस प्रक्रिया से बनी ऊर्जा कैल्विन चक्र को शक्ति देती है, जो कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड को ग्लूकोज में परिवर्तित करता है।

Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens without causing the disease itself. They typically contain a weakened or inactivated form of a germ, a piece of it such as a protein, or genetic instructions like mRNA that prompt cells to produce a harmless piece of the pathogen. The immune system responds by producing antibodies

to produce a harmless piece of the pathogen. The immune system responds by producing antibodies and memory cells. If the body later encounters the actual pathogen, the immune system can respond quickly, often preventing illness or reducing its severity. Herd immunity occurs when a large enough proportion of a population is vaccinated, slowing the spread of disease.
